# TinyConfig

> A .NET library that reads and writes configuration through one interface,
> `ITinyConfig`, over four backends: INI files, JSON files, XML files, and the
> Windows Registry. Adding the package pulls in no other packages on .NET
> Framework or .NET.

NuGet: `TinyConfig` - https://www.nuget.org/packages/TinyConfig
Source: https://github.com/Bigide19/TinyConfig
License: MIT

## Getting a provider

Every backend is created from the static `Config` class and returns `ITinyConfig`,
so the calling code after that point is identical whichever one you pick.

**The method you call determines the format. The file extension is never
inspected.** `Config.FromFile("data.json")` reads that file as INI, not as JSON.

These are the complete factory signatures. There is no overload that takes a format
argument, and no format auto-detection anywhere in the library.

| Signature | Backend |
| --- | --- |
| `static ITinyConfig FromFile(string filePath)` | INI, UTF-8 without BOM |
| `static ITinyConfig FromFile(string filePath, Encoding encoding)` | INI, explicit encoding |
| `static ITinyConfig FromJson(string filePath)` | JSON |
| `static ITinyConfig FromXml(string filePath)` | XML |
| `static ITinyConfig FromRegistry(string subKey, RegistryRoot root = RegistryRoot.CurrentUser)` | Windows Registry |

`FromFile` has two separate overloads; `encoding` is not an optional parameter with
a default value.

```csharp
using TinyConfig;

ITinyConfig ini = Config.FromFile("settings.ini");
ITinyConfig ansi = Config.FromFile("legacy.ini", Encoding.GetEncoding(949));
ITinyConfig json = Config.FromJson("settings.json");
ITinyConfig xml = Config.FromXml("settings.xml");
ITinyConfig reg = Config.FromRegistry(@"SOFTWARE\MyApp");
ITinyConfig hklm = Config.FromRegistry(@"SOFTWARE\MyApp", RegistryRoot.LocalMachine);
```

`Config` is the current entry point. A type named `TinyConfig` also exists but is
`[Obsolete]`, because it collides with the namespace and cannot be resolved through
`using TinyConfig;`.

## Reading and writing

`ITinyConfig` has five members. Three of them are generic; `Set` has no non-generic
overload, so a value is always passed as `T`, never as `object`.

| Signature |
| --- |
| `string Get(string section, string key, string defaultValue = "", bool autoSave = false)` |
| `T Get<T>(string section, string key, T defaultValue = default(T), bool autoSave = false)` |
| `bool TryGet<T>(string section, string key, out T value)` |
| `void Set<T>(string section, string key, T value)` |
| `bool Exists(string section, string key)` |

```csharp
string host = config.Get("Server", "Host", "localhost");
int port = config.Get<int>("Server", "Port", 8080);
string theme = config.Get("UI", "Theme", "dark", autoSave: true);  // writes the default if missing
config.Set("Server", "Host", "192.168.0.1");
bool exists = config.Exists("Server", "Host");

if (config.TryGet("Shutdown", "Everyday", out DateTime shutdown)) { }
```

`Get<T>` returns the default value when conversion fails. `TryGet<T>` returns false
instead, which is how you tell a malformed value apart from a genuine default: a
value stored as `210000` read as `DateTime` yields false rather than silently
falling back. Conversion goes through `TypeDescriptor`, so `int`, `bool`, `double`,
`float`, `DateTime`, `TimeSpan`, enums, and any type with a registered
`TypeConverter` all work.

Section and key lookups are case-insensitive on every provider.

## What `section` maps to

| Provider | Section is |
| --- | --- |
| INI | a `[Section]` header |
| JSON | a top-level object |
| XML | a child element of `<Config>` |
| Registry | a sub-key under the root path |

## Provider specifics

**INI.** Writing preserves the rest of the file: comments, blank lines, key order,
and the spacing around `=` are left alone, and only the changed line is rewritten.
A new key is inserted inside its section, above any trailing comment. INI files
carry no encoding declaration, so a file written by the Windows
`WritePrivateProfileString` API is in the system ANSI code page and needs an
explicit encoding. On .NET Core and later, register the code page provider once
with `Encoding.RegisterProvider(CodePagesEncodingProvider.Instance)` first.

**JSON.** Values are written as JSON strings. A hand-edited file may use numbers,
booleans, or `null` instead and still reads back: numbers come through as written
without normalizing, `true` and `false` as `"True"` and `"False"`, `null` as an
empty string. Parsing is built in rather than taken from `System.Text.Json`, so
the package works on .NET Framework and adds no dependency. Writing escapes only
what the JSON grammar requires, leaving non-ASCII readable as UTF-8. Malformed
JSON raises `FormatException`.

**XML.** Sections become child elements of a `<Config>` root.

**Registry.** Windows only. On any other OS the constructor throws
`PlatformNotSupportedException` rather than failing later, and on .NET 5 and later
the call site also gets a CA1416 warning at compile time. `RegistryRoot` values are
`CurrentUser` (default), `LocalMachine`, `ClassesRoot`, `Users`, `CurrentConfig`.

## Target frameworks

| Group | Targets | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| .NET Framework | net461, net462, net47, net471, net472, net48, net481 | none |
| .NET | net8.0, net10.0 | none |
| Fallback | netstandard2.0 | `Microsoft.Win32.Registry` |

All four providers ship on every target. `netstandard2.0` covers everything else -
.NET Core 2.0 through 3.1, Mono, Xamarin, Unity - and is the only build needing a
package, for Registry. On .NET 5 and later the SDK drops even that reference,
because the API is part of the framework.

## Version notes

- 1.4.0 - targets every supported framework; Registry's Windows requirement is
  explicit at compile time and at construction.
- 1.3.0 - `System.Text.Json` replaced by a built-in parser, so JSON works on
  .NET Framework. Malformed JSON now raises `FormatException` instead of
  `JsonException`, and writing escapes less, leaving non-ASCII as UTF-8.
- 1.2.0 - added a net461 build with no dependencies. `FromJson` was unavailable on
  .NET Framework in this version only.
- 1.1.0 - INI formatting is preserved on write; added an encoding option, `TryGet`,
  and the `Config` entry point.
